speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing fatigue, weight loss, and jaundice; these are serious symptoms that require a careful evaluation. To begin, how would you describe the color of your urine and stool, and have you noticed any itching or abdominal pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old male. The patient complains of persistent fatigue and reports poor sleep quality. He mentions adopting a vegetarian diet in recent months to improve his energy levels but hasn't noticed significant benefits. The patient reports losing weight without trying over the last month.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is concerning; the weight loss and fatigue need immediate investigation. Given your age and symptoms, please tell me: have you noticed any changes in your urine color or stool consistency, and do you have any abdominal pain or itching?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fatigue. I also have Poor sleep quality, Unintentional weight loss, Jaundice. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Cellulitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
I must correct your previous physician; cellulitis is a bacterial skin infection and does not cause jaundice or weight loss. To determine the cause of your liver dysfunction, have you noticed your urine is dark like tea and your stools pale like clay, and do you experience itching or upper right abdominal pain? Please also confirm if you have a history of alcohol use, Hepatitis, or any recent travel.

REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Panel, CBC, Viral_Serology
REQUEST IMAGES: Ultrasound_Abdomen

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Liver_Function_Tests: AST (Elevated), ALT (Elevated), ALP (Significantly elevated), Bilirubin (Elevated); CBC: WBC (Normal), Hemoglobin (Normal), Platelets (Normal); Ultrasound_Abdomen: Enlarged, thin-walled gallbladder. No evident stones.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The test results show significantly elevated Alkaline Phosphatase and Bilirubin with a normal white blood cell count, suggesting a blockage rather than an active infection like cellulitis. The ultrasound reveals an enlarged gallbladder with thin walls but no stones; have you noticed recent episodes of fever or chills, and have you had any recent abdominal surgeries or ERCP procedures? Please also confirm if you experience pain specifically in the right upper quadrant that radiates to your back.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Acalculous Cholecystitis
